plain_description.what: The anchor-free tree groups questions into category-pure cells less well than a flat mixture model. This test tries a cheap fix: re-assign each question to the nearest cell within its parent branch (a few k-means-style passes). It then measures how much of the purity gap remains, on about 3,400 held-out questions.
plain_description.why: It asks whether the tree's weaker partition can be repaired cheaply, or whether it is built into the tree approach.
plain_description.information: If the gap closed, the tree would be as good a partition as the flat model. If it did not, the cost of using a tree is real. Result: done and valid, with a partial outcome. The gap is NOT closed: it shrinks but stays below zero. Whether what remains is large cannot be read: its size sits only 0.0009 under the bar for calling it large, too close to call, so this point is descriptive only. Most of the improvement comes from just recomputing the cell centres. The refinement passes themselves are not shown to help. Results on the other re-draws are descriptive (on one of them the original gap's interval contains zero).
